fact: The bow visor and its locking mechanism failed, allowing water to flood the car deck
source: Final Report on the Capsizing on 28 September 1994 in the Baltic Sea of the Ro-Ro Passenger Vessel MV ESTONIA, Joint Accident Investigation Commission of Estonia, Finland and Sweden (1997)

fact: Hundreds of tonnes of water flooded the car deck, causing the ship to list severely (approximately 30 degrees and beyond)
source: Final Report on the MV ESTONIA disaster, Joint Accident Investigation Commission (1997), Chapter 3 — The Accident

fact: 852 people died in the sinking of the MS Estonia
source: Wikipedia, citing the Joint Accident Investigation Commission final report

fact: Engineers had warned that the bow visor design was inadequate for open-sea conditions
source: Widely documented; the Swedish government's supplementary investigation (2005) and the original JAIC report noted that the bow visor locking arrangements did not meet classification society standards for the wave loads encountered in open-sea service

fact: The Estonia sank during a storm while crossing the Baltic Sea on the night of September 27–28, 1994
source: Final Report on the MV ESTONIA disaster, Joint Accident Investigation Commission of Estonia, Finland and Sweden (1997)

fact: Ro-ro ferries with bow visor doors continued to operate on Baltic routes after the disaster
source: Widely documented; the IMO adopted amendments to SOLAS (Stockholm Agreement, 1996) to improve ro-ro ferry survivability, but ferries with bow doors continued sailing under revised safety standards
